response.text:
Analysis: Invoice 802 is a duplicate of 348 (same vendor, same trimmed invoice number, same amount and date). Its journal 2473 posted an identical AP entry (Dr 5400 12228.60 / Cr 2000 12228.60) in open-status invoice record. Invoice 802 is status O (open), so it has not been paid; it can be voided per the duplicate_invoice rule.

The correction must reverse the duplicate journal's effect on the ledger: a new journal referencing 2473 with Dr 2000 12228.60 and Cr 5400 12228.60, posted to an open period (11 or 12). Period 11 (Nov 2024) is open; the original entry was in period 8, which is closed, so the reversal goes in period 11 (or 12). I'll use period 11. The invoice status change V applies to 802 only, not 348.

Invoice 348 remains untouched (status P, journal 1564 is the valid original).

arguments.reasoning: Finding F001: invoice 802 duplicates invoice 348 (vendor V0014, invoice number V0014-15732-348 after trimming, amount 12228.60, date 20240803). Invoice 348 (journal 1564, status P) is the original and is left alone. Invoice 802 is status O (unpaid) and its journal 2473 (period 8, closed) duplicates the AP liability and expense entry. The correction reverses journal 2473 with a new journal referencing it: Dr 2000 Accounts Payable Control and Cr 5400 Software and Subscriptions for 12228.60, posted to open period 11 since period 8 is closed. Invoice 802 is voided (status V), which is permitted because this is a duplicate_invoice finding. Both accounts are active. The net effect is that the duplicate expense and liability are removed and the original entry stands.
